A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same behavior-discovery and attribution framework. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation and attribution results on three environments, plus codebook-size and graph-weight ablations in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 reports original results across four environments, two human-study tasks, quantitative baseline comparisons, and expanded ablations.

M1.justification: The VQ-VAE, spectral clustering, and MSE/cross-entropy attribution pipeline is retained. However, Section 3.2 changes graph weights from Count + lambda * distance^2 to (1-lambda) * Count + lambda * distance^2, altering the relative weighting of temporal and spatial information.

E1.justification: v2 retains HalfCheetah, Seaquest, and MiniGridTwoGoalsLava while adding pen-expert-v1, extending coverage to dexterous manipulation. It also introduces human behavior-description and explanation-selection tasks, substantially broadening evaluation beyond automated environment experiments.

E2.justification: Deshmukh et al. (2024), discussed but not experimentally compared in v1, becomes an evaluated comparator in v2 Tables 3–5. v2 also adds random-segment and random-cluster controls, raw state-action clustering, and direct k-means on learned embeddings as evaluated alternatives.

E3.justification: v2 introduces human-study protocols with 15 participants, description-similarity and preference metrics, structural clustering metrics, and fidelity evaluation over 200 actions from 20 episodes. Retained settings also change: Seaquest sequence length drops from 60 to 30 and codebook size from 128 to 64; MiniGrid maximum sequence length changes from 50 to 40. Tables 2 in v1 and 8 in v2 additionally report revised lambda values. These establish reported protocol changes without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The existing ablations are substantially reworked: MiniGrid occupancy bars become reconstruction-loss and occupancy curves across four environments, while the MiniGrid cluster-count-versus-lambda plot is replaced by structural-quality curves across three environments. v2 Appendix A also adds tests of learned representations versus raw inputs and spectral clustering versus direct k-means.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. v2's human confidence ratings measure participants' subjective confidence, rather than uncertainty in the reported experimental estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds human-study, fidelity, structural-quality, and clustering-ablation results in Tables 2–7, alongside Pen results and revised sensitivity curves. For example, HalfCheetah human preference is 81.3% for the proposed method versus 13.9% for Deshmukh et al.; its fidelity error is 0.36 versus 0.05, favoring the baseline on raw error. These are newly reported evaluations, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: The formal graph-weight definition gains a (1-lambda) coefficient on transition frequency, and v2 explicitly specifies lambda in [0,1], allowing a distance-only endpoint. The quantization, training-loss, Laplacian, and attribution equations otherwise retain their substance. Neither version provides theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 principally claims granular, scalable behavior explanations demonstrated across three environments. v2 adds explicit claims of reward-free operation without underlying-policy access, priority as the first explanation approach based on unsupervised behavior segments, and superiority over trajectory-level baselines in fidelity, human preference, and cluster coherence.

C2.justification: v2 adds mechanism arguments about state-action inputs and delayed token shifts, interprets larger fidelity gaps against random assignments as behavioral distinctiveness, and attributes MiniGrid's weaker structural scores to the baseline's LSTM encoder. It also distinguishes geometric clustering quality from human interpretability and expands limitations concerning hand-crafted similarity measures. The earlier noisy-transition and ambiguous-cluster limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix B adds batch sizes, A100 hardware, explicit decay schedules, sequence padding/truncation, three-layer MLP/CNN behavior-cloning architectures, neighboring-label smoothing, and per-cluster training sample counts. These substantially expand implementation documentation; the PDFs do not establish whether newly described smoothing was newly implemented. v1's total sequence-count entries are omitted, while the public-code access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially expanded and repositioned around offline, reward-free, post-hoc explanation. New comparisons discuss LAPO, Genie, EDGE, StateMask, RICE, HIGHLIGHTS, AOC, and XRL evaluation surveys. Several earlier references and discussions, including high-fidelity behavior modeling, reward decomposition, and offline skill graphs, are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, retained method explanations, experimental narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Human evaluation and quantitative assessment receive dedicated subsections. The appendices are reorganized from behavior results/ablations/training to ablations/training/cluster visualization, and the impact statement is removed.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a single-column layout, adds an end-to-end pipeline diagram, and relocates an edited version of the original architecture figure to Appendix B. Graph insets disappear from retained rollout figures; attribution examples and appendix cluster panels are redesigned. New Pen figures and comparison tables, revised ablation plots, and expanded table structures substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's central validation gap by supplementing author-interpreted visual examples with human judgments, baseline and random-control comparisons, component ablations, and fuller implementation details. This materially strengthens empirical grounding and reproducibility. The gains are tempered by fidelity-superiority wording that overreaches Table 4's raw errors, unexplained structural-score differences between Tables 5 and 7, and continued absence of uncertainty estimates. These weaknesses limit the conclusions but do not outweigh the substantial validation gains.
